problem: The sentence 'Histograms are non-negative, so cosine is common in text and audio retrieval' gives a wrong reason. Non-negativity is not why cosine is used; cosine is used because it ignores vector length, which matters when histograms or term counts have different totals. It also jumps from image histograms to text and audio without saying so.
fix: For non-negative vectors the angle θ lies between 0° and 90°. Cosine ignores vector length, so it suits histograms whose bins add up to different totals, and it is also the usual measure for term-count vectors in text retrieval.

where: Section 3, paragraph on precision and recall
problem: 'A system that returns one safe item has high precision and low recall' — 'safe item' is undefined and precision is high only if that one item is actually relevant.
fix: A system that returns a single relevant item has precision 1 and very low recall; a system that returns every item in the database has recall 1 and low precision.

problem: 'recall looks at what was missed' is ambiguous; a student can read it as 'recall counts the missed items', but recall counts the relevant items that were found.
fix: Precision looks at the returned list; recall looks at how much of the relevant set was found, that is, at what was not missed.

problem: 'pixels-derived features' is awkward and unclear wording.
fix: 'pixel-derived features' or 'features computed from the image pixels'.
